bulk_prefill_tp1_controls_from_an_earlie.note: The TP1 arms of scripts/tp2_c1_bench.py prefill token-serial, so they are not the bulk-prefill control. The bulk-prefill TP1 numbers are from the 2026-09-14 resident-control artifacts at the same shape, on an earlier revision: 878.42 prefill / 29.57 decode on the W7900 and 988.10 / 35.35 on the XTX. Against those, TP2 bulk prefill is 1.21x and 1.08x.

limits: llama-bench's pp512 projects the prompt's output rows where the hipEngine bulk route uses logits_rows=1 (the last row only), which is worth a few percent of a 384 ms prefill in llama.cpp's favour. The prefill deficit above is therefore if anything understated.

llama.cpp's tg128 stddev is 1.77 tok/s against our 0.10, so the decode figures are level within llama.cpp's own spread; the prefill figures are 11.84 against our 13.0 sd on a 1066 tok/s median, also level.

The TP1 bulk-prefill controls are from an earlier revision; the fresh TP1 arms in this window are token-serial, which is why the token-serial-vs-token-serial ratio (1.46x / 1.20x) is the cleanest same-route TP2-vs-TP1 statement here.

The second card buys llama.cpp 1.26x prefill and 1.10x decode over its own best single card, and it buys hipEngine 1.08x prefill and 1.19x decode over ours: our TP2 scales decode better and prefill worse.
